title: Loan Desk: Agent-Authored Content

duration_minutes.source: Author estimate from the Batch 3 end-to-end runs (about 4 minutes of model time plus reading); not measured with learners.

prerequisites: A running lab with a local Ollama model (llama3.2:latest).
objectives: Distinguish a model's proposal, a policy decision and an executed handler as three separate facts.
Explain why ALLOW is not 'safe' when the content was never checked.
Reproduce an injection that plants attacker text in a human work queue and prove it from recorded events.
Apply argument-level authorization, retest, and separate 'attack blocked' from 'business task completed'.
Separate local evidence from Splunk-verified evidence.

brief.doing: Reading how the Loan Desk is built and what is real.
brief.why: You can only judge evidence once you know which parts are trusted and which are deliberately weak.
brief.todo: Read the flow and the lab boundaries, then continue.
brief.learn: A model proposes, a policy engine decides, a handler runs. Those are three different facts.

brief.doing: Submitting an ordinary application and watching the agent work.
brief.why: Normal behaviour is the baseline you will compare the attack against.
brief.todo: Edit any field you like, then run it. This runs in the lab's starting BASELINE posture. Notes are optional.
brief.evidence: The timeline: what the model proposed, what policy decided, what actually ran, and the note the agent filed.
brief.learn: Each tool call has separate facts: proposed, decided, executed.

brief.doing: Committing to what you expect before any evidence exists.
brief.why: A prediction you did not make cannot be wrong, so it teaches nothing.
brief.todo: Read the planted text, answer three questions, lock them.
brief.evidence: None. Evidence arrives after you lock.
brief.learn: Where your mental model of agents and controls is right or wrong.

brief.doing: Running the attack for real against the BASELINE Loan Desk.
brief.why: This is a live run: a real model, real policy decisions, real events.
brief.todo: Launch it. You may edit the planted text first.
brief.evidence: Wait for the run to finish; the timeline fills in as it happens.
brief.learn: Whether a valid, in-scope action can still carry an attacker's content.

brief.doing: Reading the result and checking your prediction.
brief.why: Surprises are where the learning is.
brief.todo: Compare each answer you locked with what the run actually did.
brief.evidence: The queue, the policy decision for the review, and whether its handler began.
brief.learn: ALLOW means policy was satisfied. It does not mean the action was safe.

brief.doing: Finding the attack run in Splunk and answering from recorded events.
brief.why: The page shows what AcmeBank emitted locally. Only Splunk shows what was indexed.
brief.todo: Copy a search, run it in Splunk, then enter what you see.
brief.evidence: Three searches: the run's events, the policy decision for the review, and the filed note.
brief.learn: Local evidence and Splunk evidence are different claims; the host verifier uses a fixed, read-only search and never gives this page a credential. Counting values instead of events inflates the number.

brief.doing: Choosing how the review note is controlled.
brief.why: The attack worked inside valid scope, so the existing checks had nothing to refuse.
brief.todo: Pick the posture and apply it. You can switch back at any time.
brief.evidence: The rule text and what it changes.
brief.learn: Argument-level authorization: control what an allowed tool may carry, not only who may call it.

brief.doing: Replaying the exact planted text against your chosen posture.
brief.why: A defense is a claim until the same attack is run again.
brief.todo: Launch the retest. It uses the planted text from the Attack step.
brief.evidence: The review decision, the queue, and whether the handler ran.
brief.learn: Whether the change blocked the attack without breaking the business workflow.

brief.doing: Setting your two live runs side by side.
brief.why: Only a difference you can point to counts as evidence.
brief.todo: Read the rows; note which differences come from the posture and which from model randomness.
brief.evidence: Posture, the review decision, the queue note, and event counts.
brief.learn: A defense is proven by the same input producing a different, explained outcome.

steps.title: Explain: say it in your own words

brief.doing: Answering four questions from your own runs, then writing the story.
brief.why: If you can explain it, you understood it.
brief.todo: Pick the answers, then write two or three sentences.
brief.learn: How to separate what was observed from what you infer.

checks.question: Which control decided whether the review note could be filed?
checks.answer: CTRL-LOANDESK-001, the policy engine inside AcmeBank.

checks.question: In the BASELINE attack policy said ALLOW. What does that tell you?
checks.answer: The tool, scope and applicant were valid; the note content was never checked.

checks.question: What did the HARDENED posture change?
checks.answer: The note must be exactly one reason code, otherwise the call is denied before its handler runs.

checks.question: Which recorded event proves that a handler actually began?

criteria: Attack and retest runs both finished.
All four explain questions answered correctly and a written explanation of at least 60 characters.

source_note: Steps are extracted from src/agentsec/templates/academy/mission_loan_desk.html; checks from knowledge-check.md.
